heard: A billion-year-old star is glowing with elements that decay in decades. Our Sun is mostly hydrogen, with heavy elements making up less than 1%. Located 356 light-years away in Centaurus, P. Arzybilski's star completely flips that solar recipe. In 1961, astronomer and Tony P. Arzybilski found rare earth metals like holmium enriched by 1,000 times solar levels. Later studies reported short-lived actinides like promethium, an unstable element that decays in under 18 years. That sparked wild theories, including alien civilizations dumping radioactive nuclear waste into their sun. However, a 2023 study showed overlapping spectral lines might explain away those short-lived elements. Yet the mystery of this slow-spinning cosmic anomaly remains unsolved.
